## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sīlavīmaṁsanajātaka* (Ja 305), titled in English as "A Test of Virtue," is a canonical Jātaka tale preserved in the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework, the Buddha delivered this teaching while residing at Jetavana regarding the restraint of defilements (*kilesaniggaha*), specifically prompted by five hundred resident monks who had fallen into sensual thoughts during the middle watch of the night [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. The commentary notes that the full background story is related in the *Pānīyajātaka* of the Eleventh Book (*Ekādasanipāta*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. The canonical verse opens with the incipit *N'atthi loke raho nāma* ("There is no secrecy in the world") [Fausböll 1883]. At the end of the exposition, the five hundred monks achieved arahantship, and the Buddha identified the previous births (*samodhāna*), revealing that the teacher of that time was Sāriputta and the wise youth (*paṇḍitamāṇavo*) was the Bodhisatta [Fausböll 1883].

In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text with sections of Āryaśūra's Sanskrit *Jātakamālā*, though these are machine alignments rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
